::: {#exm-neighborhood}
#### Neighborhoods with a loop and parallel edges

In the graph of @exm-loop-parallel,

$$
N(p) = \set{p, q}, \qquad N(q) = \set{p, r}, \qquad N(r) = \set{q, s}, \qquad N(s) = \set{r}.
$$

The loop at $p$ puts $p$ in its own neighborhood (@def-neighborhood).
The two parallel edges joining $q$ and $r$ put $r$ in $N(q)$ only once, since $N(q)$ is a set.

:::
